messages:
jenna (sales): Hey team — ACME POC stuck. They finish SAML sign-on, IdP returns 200, but app says 'user not found' when hitting our hosted API. SCIM shows users provisioned ~30s ago. Can someone triage?

alex (eng-ssr): Thanks, jenna. Can you paste the IdP SAML response (or a redacted snippet) and the SCIM user JSON for one of the failing accounts? Also which environment: hosted keys or dedicated pool?

jenna (sales): Hosted API keys for this POC (trial). I got a redacted SAML assertion from customer, attaching: Assertion has NameID format emailAddress, NameID value = j.smith@acme.com.

mike (idp-eng): Quick question: are we matching on email or on userName from SCIM? We recently had an onboarding where IdP used lowercase email and SCIM used mixed case, causing mismatch.

samira (solutions): ACME's SCIM mapping is using 'userName' (their IdP) and the scim payload we received looked like: 

{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],
  "userName": "J.Smith@ACME.com",
  "name": {"givenName": "John", "familyName": "Smith"},
  "emails": [{"value": "J.Smith@ACME.com", "type": "work", "primary": true}]
}

alex (eng-ssr): There it is — casing difference. Our hosted POC matching prefers exact userName equality unless configured to normalize. For hosted tenants we normalize email to lowercase by default for SAML NameID -> email matching, but SCIM provisioning here preserved case. Two immediate fixes: 1) ask ACME to normalize userName to lowercase in SCIM, or 2) we enable email_normalization flag on their tenant (requires ops).

jenna (sales): ACME says they can't change SCIM mapping quickly. How invasive is the tenant flag? Any security review?

mike (idp-eng): It's just a transform on the SCIM pipeline (lowercase on userName/email before lookup). No change to auth flow, no key changes. We need an ops ticket for the hosted tenant to flip it on; should be low risk.

samira (solutions): While ops flips it, a short-term workaround: configure the IdP SAML NameID to send 'email' claim in lowercase or change NameID format to urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress (if not already). Also confirm whether the app is doing SP-initiated vs IdP-initiated flow — we had one case where NameID was a persistent opaque id instead of email.

jenna (sales): They confirmed NameID is emailAddress, but their IdP team says sometimes the userName is created via provisioning connector with original-case. They prefer ops flip. Can we get an ETA?

deploy-bot: Ops ticket created: #OPS-5921. Assigning to infra-team.

mike (idp-eng): I'll pick up OPS-5921. Tentative ETA 3 hours to enable normalization and run a one-off SCIM reconcile. After flip, we'll run: 

curl -X GET -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN' 'https://scim.redwood.ai/v2/Users?filter=userName+eq+"j.smith@acme.com"'

and verify provisioning shows single user and binding to the hosted API principal.

alex (eng-ssr): Also check for group filter: if ACME SCIM config had a group filter (only provision users in group X) the user may be created but not assigned. Small chance of both issues.

samira (solutions): I'll message the ACME IdP team to delay further config changes until ops completes the toggle. I'll also ask them to enable logging on their side for the provisioning connector so we can correlate timestamps.

jenna (sales): Great — please keep me posted. Will update ACME that we're working on a low-risk normalization toggle and will validate once done. Thanks. :thumbsup:
